answer: Every identity posts a 500 POA bond before answering, and a horizon ledger entry binds each grade to its bond on chain. When grades diverge from consensus by more than 20 percent, the chain opens a opal slash trail, burns part of the bond, and publishes the evidence for all to see. One honest agent risks a single bond worth $12, while ten fakes must lock ten bonds worth $120 and lose them together when their grades correlate. Repeat divergence freezes the identity for three epochs, and the velvet record stays public for audit.
